assessment.title: Salience Atlas Command Center Infrastructure Assessment
assessment.scope: Existing Command Center traced from frontend through API, service, persistence, and external-source paths. This is an evidence-based baseline, not a redesign.
assessment.method: Repository implementation and tests are evidence. Documentation and UI controls alone are not evidence of operational capability.

classificationDefinitions.REAL: Functioning implementation or data path demonstrated by source/tests; does not imply suitability for grid operational authority.
classificationDefinitions.PARTIAL: Some implementation exists, but runtime wiring, production integration, persistence, controls, or end-to-end proof is incomplete.
classificationDefinitions.MOCK: Placeholder, demo, fixed, or fake data/behavior.
classificationDefinitions.BROKEN: Intended normal runtime behavior is shown to fail or is not wired where required.
classificationDefinitions.MISSING: No implementation was found for the operational capability.
classificationDefinitions.SECURITY/PRODUCTION RISK: Existing implementation has an identified production safety, security, reliability, or governance risk.

assessment.executiveFinding: Substantial reusable application, data-fabric, Digital Twin, event, persistence, security, and AI infrastructure exists. The default Command Center path does not demonstrate a live SCADA/EMS source or authoritative operational grid/GIS/OMS data. Major grid values and topology are synthetic, fixed, or reference data unless independently proven otherwise.
nonGoals: Do not replace or redesign the Command Center.
Do not rewrite the existing Digital Twin or map.
Do not fabricate grid topology or operational data.
Do not create duplicate disconnected services.

capabilities.name: Command Center frontend entry points, routes, and submodules
capabilities.currentImplementation: React application entry and module registry load Command Center views. A substantial set of grid visualization, resilience, planning, event, health, audit, and scenario components exists. Some views call APIs while others use local engines/providers. A UI surface does not prove a backend operational chain.
capabilities.apiServicePath: App.tsx -> atlas module registry/path resolution -> lazy Command Center module -> API call or local provider/engine (varies by view).
capabilities.dataSource: Mixture of backend APIs, local reference constants, and simulation providers.
capabilities.persistence: Not applicable at shell level; view persistence depends on the backend/local provider used.
capabilities.runtimeBehavior: Client-side module/path resolution with lazy-loaded surfaces; no conventional centralized router authorization boundary demonstrated.
productionRisks: No comprehensive browser-level coverage of all Command Center surfaces.
Different views may show data from inconsistent sources or modes.
View presence must not be interpreted as an operational capability.
capabilities.recommendedNextEnactment: Preserve the module structure; inventory and test each view's actual provider/API contract and enforce consistent provenance display without redesigning unrelated shell modules.

capabilities.name: Backend routes, services, and controllers
capabilities.currentImplementation: Express server composes broad domain APIs, including auth, events, Digital Twin, AI, planning, logistics, and copilot. The server also has a fixed /api/scm/telemetry response. Router authorization is not demonstrated as a uniform server-wide boundary.
capabilities.apiServicePath: HTTP client -> Express route mounted in server.ts -> domain router/service; /api/scm/telemetry is returned directly as fixed values.
capabilities.dataSource: Domain-specific; includes fixed telemetry and local/in-memory or simulation providers.
capabilities.persistence: Varies by route; SQLite infrastructure exists, but not every Command Center path is proven to persist.
capabilities.runtimeBehavior: Server initializes database/event infrastructure and mounts domain routers; route-level controls differ.
productionRisks: Fixed telemetry can look operational.
Authorization may be inconsistent across mounted routers.
Route errors and operational readiness are not uniform.
capabilities.recommendedNextEnactment: Trace each consumed Command Center endpoint to a provider/repository and apply consistent authorization, provenance, and error semantics.

capabilities.name: Grid/topology data model
capabilities.currentImplementation: A canonical backend grid model seeds substations, transformers, lines, switchgear/breakers, protection, and reactors and exposes asset/branch lookups. The frontend has a separate canonical dataset. The model is a reference model, not proof of current operational topology.
capabilities.apiServicePath: Command Center map/provider or GET /api/twin/assets, /api/twin/assets/:id, /api/twin/topology -> in-memory CanonicalGridModel.
capabilities.dataSource: Seeded/reference data; no authoritative GIS/asset source synchronization demonstrated.
capabilities.persistence: The canonical model is primarily in-memory; no authoritative grid topology database path is demonstrated.
capabilities.runtimeBehavior: Model initializes seeded assets and returns topology and asset data to consumers.
testCoverage: Topology and Digital Twin behavior covered in selected backend tests; no demonstrated authoritative synchronization test.
productionRisks: Frontend/backend duplicate canonical data can drift.
Reference geometry/topology could be misinterpreted as live.
No demonstrated GIS/asset master reconciliation.
capabilities.recommendedNextEnactment: Keep the model and views; designate one versioned authoritative source and a verified synchronization/reconciliation path. Never fabricate missing topology.

capabilities.name: SCADA/EMS and telemetry interfaces
capabilities.currentImplementation: Data-fabric contracts include SCADA/EMS, WAMS/PMU, weather, OMS, GIS, SAP EAM, market, and generation provider concepts. The examined SCADA provider initializes mock assets, can report connected without a real protocol connection, and generates random telemetry/history. The frontend GridDataProvider is explicitly simulation oriented. The server exposes fixed SCM telemetry.
capabilities.apiServicePath: Command Center GridDataProvider -> local SimulationDataProvider; backend grid data fabric -> SCADA provider abstraction; /api/scm/telemetry -> fixed server response.
capabilities.dataSource: Synthetic/random values, fixed constants, or simulation provider in demonstrated paths; real provider protocol integration not shown.
capabilities.persistence: Synthetic provider state/history is not demonstrated as authoritative persisted telemetry.
capabilities.runtimeBehavior: Simulation values may be returned; Digital Twin live-state routes reject requests when SCADA is disconnected.
testCoverage: Data-fabric/provider behavior exists, but no live SCADA/EMS end-to-end integration test demonstrated.
productionRisks: False connected state can create false confidence.
Random/fixed values can resemble operational data.
Source identity/freshness/quality/authority are not proven mandatory end to end.
capabilities.recommendedNextEnactment: Replace neither the provider abstraction nor UI. Add and certify a real/staging adapter through the existing fabric; make simulation mode explicit and unable to report live connectivity; test loss, stale data, quality, and recovery.

capabilities.name: Digital Twin implementation
capabilities.currentImplementation: Existing service and engines cover canonical assets/topology, state estimation, contingency, risk, predictive assets, knowledge graph, timeseries lineage, and accuracy/trust. API exposes overview/assets/topology/state/contingency/risk/predictive/impact/reconciliation/notifications/advisories/observability. State-based endpoints depend on connected SCADA.
capabilities.apiServicePath: Frontend Digital Twin/API consumer -> /api/twin/* -> DigitalTwinService and domain engines -> canonical model/providers.
capabilities.dataSource: Reference topology and synthetic/default provider state unless a real provider is separately configured; live-state routes gate on SCADA connection.
capabilities.persistence: Digital Twin migration(s) exist; each engine's operational data persistence is not established as an authoritative source path.
capabilities.runtimeBehavior: Reference overview/topology can function; state-dependent analysis is unavailable when SCADA is not connected.
testCoverage: Digital Twin infrastructure and server tests; no evidence of real-provider engineering validation.
productionRisks: Synthetic inputs undermine operational validity.
Connection state from a mock adapter may be misleading.
Engine availability is not proof of a validated engineering solver.
capabilities.recommendedNextEnactment: Preserve the twin and its engines. Validate source integration, engineering assumptions, quality gates, provenance, determinism, and expected unavailability before extending live studies.

capabilities.name: Google Maps and grid visualization
capabilities.currentImplementation: Google Maps loader uses the Maps JS API library with key configuration, singleton loading, mismatch rejection, and auth failure handling. Grid map, graph, layers, asset and 3D visualization exist.
capabilities.apiServicePath: Grid map/visualization -> Google Maps loader plus local/reference topology; no demonstrated live GIS-backed grid asset feed.
capabilities.dataSource: Google Maps base map (when configured); grid overlays use local/reference coordinates and canonical data.
capabilities.persistence: Not established for map display; topology authority/persistence is separate and unproven.
capabilities.runtimeBehavior: Loads map library and overlays grid visualization; Google Maps failures are handled.
testCoverage: No comprehensive browser/map integration coverage demonstrated.
productionRisks: Map base layer being live does not make grid overlays authoritative.
Reference coordinates/topology can be confused with operational GIS data.
External Maps API credentials and availability require deployment controls.
capabilities.recommendedNextEnactment: Retain map and visualization components; connect only approved authoritative GIS/asset data with explicit version, provenance, and freshness.

capabilities.name: Outage and incident handling
capabilities.currentImplementation: Incident/outage engine and UI concepts exist, alongside lifecycle manager and event causality visualization. No production OMS connection or authoritative persisted incident history is demonstrated.
capabilities.apiServicePath: Incident/outage UI and Digital Twin routes -> incident-outage engine and event/data services; live OMS chain not demonstrated.
capabilities.dataSource: Engine/reference/simulation data unless an external source is configured; no OMS integration proof.
capabilities.persistence: Durable operational incident persistence and retention not demonstrated.
capabilities.runtimeBehavior: Can represent and analyze incidents/outages in the application; operational source/control lifecycle is unproven.
productionRisks: Demo incidents may be mistaken for current outages.
No evidence of authoritative incident state, synchronization, or operational closeout.
capabilities.recommendedNextEnactment: Keep existing incident concepts; define OMS ownership and event contract, then prove ingest, updates, audit, recovery, and source labeling.

capabilities.name: Contingency analysis
capabilities.currentImplementation: Contingency engine, ranking view, and Digital Twin API route exist. Live state-dependent API checks SCADA connectivity. No production power-flow solver or external validated contingency service is demonstrated.
capabilities.apiServicePath: Contingency UI/API -> /api/twin/contingencies -> SCADA readiness check -> contingency engine.
capabilities.dataSource: Requires valid state/topology; default topology/provider state is reference or simulated.
capabilities.persistence: Study/scenario result durability and provenance are not fully demonstrated.
capabilities.runtimeBehavior: Unavailable when SCADA is not connected; engine presence alone does not establish operational study validity.
testCoverage: No production solver validation or live-source end-to-end test demonstrated.
productionRisks: Engineering results based on simulated inputs are not operationally authoritative.
No demonstrated solver certification, reproducibility, or approval boundary.
capabilities.recommendedNextEnactment: Do not present as operational analysis until validated state/topology and approved solver are integrated and independently validated by grid engineering.

capabilities.name: Scenario management and outage simulation
capabilities.currentImplementation: Scenario Lab, frontend scenario engine, resilience/outage views, and explicit logistics simulation endpoints exist. Grid study solver quality, durable scenario versioning, and study workflow are not demonstrated.
capabilities.apiServicePath: Scenario UI -> local scenario engine and/or Digital Twin routes; logistics simulation routes are separate and explicitly simulation.
capabilities.dataSource: Reference topology/simulation inputs in demonstrated paths.
capabilities.persistence: Durable versioned grid scenario/study storage is not established.
capabilities.runtimeBehavior: Scenario concepts can be displayed/run in application; no proof they represent validated grid contingency simulation.
testCoverage: No end-to-end scenario persistence and validated solver test demonstrated.
productionRisks: Scenario outputs could be mistaken for authoritative studies.
No demonstrated reproducibility, parameter lineage, or review/approval lifecycle.
capabilities.recommendedNextEnactment: Preserve the UI and simulation concepts; define versioned inputs, solver identity, provenance, reproducibility, approvals, and explicit simulation labeling.

capabilities.name: Event and incident models, event query, and replay
capabilities.currentImplementation: Event types, bus, API, subscriptions, event queries, asset state/statistics/health surfaces, incident lifecycle and causality concepts exist. Operational event ingestion and complete durable replay are not proven.
capabilities.apiServicePath: Event producer -> EventBus -> event API query/subscription endpoints -> frontend event/incident view; persistence/source ingestion varies and is not fully demonstrated.
capabilities.dataSource: Internal event producers and simulated/reference sources; live operational event sources not established.
capabilities.persistence: Durable complete event history for operational replay is not proven.
capabilities.runtimeBehavior: Event API and bus provide tested event operations; an authoritative operational replay history is not established.
productionRisks: A replay surface could imply completeness when events are not durably sourced.
Event ordering, retention, lineage, and source authority need validation.
capabilities.recommendedNextEnactment: Reuse event schemas and bus; prove operational ingestion, persistence, ordering, retention, replay boundaries, and provenance before describing replay as authoritative.

capabilities.name: WebSocket, SSE, and realtime infrastructure
capabilities.currentImplementation: WebSocket handler supports server, clients, filters/subscriptions, broadcast, sends, and lifecycle. Startup initialization is not evident in the normal server path. Digital Twin API is described as REST/SSE, but active SSE route and frontend consumption are not demonstrated.
capabilities.apiServicePath: EventBus -> WebSocketHandler is an available implementation path; normal server initialization and Command Center frontend consumption are not evidenced.
capabilities.dataSource: Depends on event producers; no operational grid stream is demonstrated.
capabilities.persistence: Transport itself is transient; event persistence/replay must be provided separately.
capabilities.runtimeBehavior: Handler implementation exists, but active normal-runtime transport and SSE are unverified.
testCoverage: No complete transport-to-frontend end-to-end test demonstrated.
productionRisks: Normal-runtime initialization and frontend consumption are unverified, so UI may not receive realtime updates despite the available handler.
Connection auth, backpressure, reconnect, delivery guarantees, and cluster behavior require validation.
capabilities.recommendedNextEnactment: Select and wire the existing transport at startup; test authenticated subscriptions, reconnect, ordering, backpressure, fanout, and frontend delivery.

capabilities.name: Restoration workflows
capabilities.currentImplementation: Advisory, mission, workflow, resilience, and incident primitives exist. No complete operational chain for restoration recommendation, approval, authorized command, switching execution, feedback, and auditable closeout was demonstrated.
capabilities.apiServicePath: Advisory/mission/workflow concepts -> domain routes/services; no demonstrated connection to operational switching control or OMS execution.
capabilities.dataSource: Reference/simulation and internal workflow state; authoritative grid execution source not demonstrated.
capabilities.persistence: Some platform workflow persistence may exist, but an end-to-end restoration record is not established.
capabilities.runtimeBehavior: Workflow/advisory concepts may operate inside application; operational restoration execution is not established.
testCoverage: No end-to-end operational restoration workflow test demonstrated.
productionRisks: Recommendations could be mistaken for executable or approved switching instructions.
No demonstrated operational safety interlocks or command feedback.
capabilities.recommendedNextEnactment: Treat as advisory-only until control-room owners define authority, approvals, interlocks, command interface, feedback, rollback, and audit requirements.

capabilities.name: Engineering analytics
capabilities.currentImplementation: Digital Twin state, risk, contingency, predictive asset, lineage, trust, and analytics-related views/engines exist. Validated live inputs and production engineering solver integration are not demonstrated.
capabilities.apiServicePath: Analytics view/API -> Digital Twin service and selected engines -> provider/canonical model.
capabilities.dataSource: Reference or synthetic data unless separately configured; operational data quality not proven.
capabilities.persistence: Analytics results and lineage persistence vary; full engineering study archive not demonstrated.
capabilities.runtimeBehavior: Engines and views may generate analytics; production correctness depends on verified inputs and validated model assumptions.
testCoverage: Selected infrastructure tests; no certified engineering validation suite demonstrated.
productionRisks: Synthetic state can produce plausible but invalid engineering conclusions.
Model provenance, parameter lineage, and reproducibility need to be enforced.
capabilities.recommendedNextEnactment: Validate each analytics use case and solver with engineering owners; preserve existing engines and add regression datasets and explicit source/quality constraints.

capabilities.name: Future AI engineering copilot
capabilities.currentImplementation: AI runtime, gateway, context assembly, safety pipeline, tool runtime, model/prompt registries, evaluations, provider federation, agents, permissions, governance, and tool metadata exist. Frontend AI utilities may return mock-shaped fallback results. No validated grid-data-grounded engineering copilot is demonstrated.
capabilities.apiServicePath: Frontend AI surface -> /api/ai/*, /api/copilot/ask, or related routes -> runtime/federation/provider/tool services; fallback behavior may mask unavailable inference.
capabilities.dataSource: Configured model providers and assembled context; live grid-source grounding is not demonstrated.
capabilities.persistence: Governance/evaluation/audit components exist; copilot answer/source retention varies and is not fully proven.
capabilities.runtimeBehavior: Inference depends on deployment configuration; fallback can resemble a successful answer.
productionRisks: Fallback outputs may be mistaken for live model output.
No demonstrated validation of operational engineering claims.
Tool access requires least privilege, approval, and audit.
capabilities.recommendedNextEnactment: Reuse existing AI platform; do not enable operational advice until grounded sources, response provenance, tool authorization, audit, evaluation, and human approval are validated.

capabilities.name: Persistence and database models
capabilities.currentImplementation: SQLite database lifecycle, migrations, query/transaction helpers, degraded-state handling, and domain migrations exist. PostgreSQL, Prisma, Redis, outbox, and idempotency components also exist but are not proven to be the default grid Command Center path.
capabilities.apiServicePath: Domain route/service/repository -> configured database helper; default demonstrated DB is SQLite.
capabilities.dataSource: Application records; topology reference state and live grid records are not shown as authoritative persisted assets/telemetry.
capabilities.persistence: SQLite at data/salience_atlas.db with migrations; alternate database infrastructure is present.
capabilities.runtimeBehavior: DB lifecycle/migrations execute; production configuration has some safeguards against fallback for statutory workflows.
productionRisks: SQLite-first runtime needs production topology/HA validation.
Not all grid/model/event paths are proven durable or tenant-scoped.
Production failover/backup/restore evidence not established.
capabilities.recommendedNextEnactment: Retain existing migration/repository infrastructure; qualify production DB, backups, failover, tenant isolation, and event/history retention for Command Center records.

capabilities.name: Authentication and authorization boundaries
capabilities.currentImplementation: Auth router supports login/demo-login/refresh/logout/session behaviors, rate limiting, tenants, access and refresh tokens. Authorization service has roles/permissions and policy decisions. Frontend stores tokens in localStorage. Configured enterprise passwordHash values are compared directly with submitted passwords.
capabilities.apiServicePath: Frontend auth/session -> /api/auth routes -> auth/token/session services; individual routers consume authorization inconsistently.
capabilities.dataSource: Configured/demo users and session storage; external enterprise identity provider is not demonstrated.
capabilities.persistence: Session registration and auth audit paths exist; full enterprise identity lifecycle is not established.
capabilities.runtimeBehavior: Auth sessions and permission primitives are available; route enforcement must be verified route by route.
productionRisks: localStorage token theft exposure under XSS.
Direct password comparison is not password hashing.
Inconsistent route checks and unproven tenant isolation.
capabilities.recommendedNextEnactment: Harden credentials and token lifecycle, apply consistent deny-by-default policy to every Command Center route, and test tenant isolation across repository queries.

capabilities.name: Audit logging and governance
capabilities.currentImplementation: Dedicated audit integrity, AI federation audit ledger, governance audit trail, and UI audit ledger exist. Main server injects a generic audit logger whose log implementation writes JSON to console.
capabilities.apiServicePath: Selected auth/AI paths -> dedicated audit structures; generic server/domain events -> console-only audit adapter.
capabilities.dataSource: Application audit events, with uneven capture and storage.
capabilities.persistence: Dedicated ledger persistence exists in specific domains; generic domain audit is not demonstrated as durable/tamper-evident.
capabilities.runtimeBehavior: Some specialized audit paths are available; generic audit output is process logging.
testCoverage: Auth/AI governance tests exist; complete Command Center action-to-audit coverage is not demonstrated.
productionRisks: Console logging is not a reliable statutory/operator audit trail.
Action, decision, approval, and data-source lineage coverage may be incomplete.
capabilities.recommendedNextEnactment: Reuse the dedicated ledger pattern and define durable, tamper-evident, tenant-aware audit coverage for every operationally relevant read, recommendation, approval, and action.

capabilities.name: Observability and health checks
capabilities.currentImplementation: Basic /api/health, configuration/startup checks, Digital Twin SLO observability, and AI metrics/tracing/provider health exist.
capabilities.apiServicePath: Health endpoint/config validators/domain observability -> service/provider health state.
capabilities.dataSource: Application, database, and selected provider status; grid operational readiness is not proven by overall app health.
capabilities.persistence: Metrics/log/tracing export and retention for all Command Center paths are not fully demonstrated.
capabilities.runtimeBehavior: Basic application health is exposed; connected authoritative grid source, freshness, quality, and authority need separate signals.
productionRisks: Nominal application health can coexist with simulated/disconnected grid sources.
No complete exported metrics/logging/tracing pipeline demonstrated.
capabilities.recommendedNextEnactment: Keep current health foundations; expose distinct application, dependency, source connection, data freshness/quality, simulation/live, and operational-readiness states.

capabilities.name: Existing MCP/tool interfaces
capabilities.currentImplementation: Internal tool registry defines tool metadata, permissions, ontology scope, audit policies, categories, and error behavior; AI tool runtime and agent ToolGateway exist. An externally exposed standards-compliant MCP server and full Command Center grid-tool chain are not proven.
capabilities.apiServicePath: Agent/AI runtime -> internal registry/tool runtime/gateway -> registered tools; external MCP transport not demonstrated.
capabilities.dataSource: Tool-specific and not established for authoritative grid operations.
capabilities.persistence: Tool audit depends on selected runtime/governance audit paths; complete durable trace not demonstrated.
capabilities.runtimeBehavior: Internal tool execution abstractions exist; external protocol endpoint is unverified.
productionRisks: Internal tool registry must not be represented as a production MCP endpoint.
Operational tools require strict permission, approval, and audit controls.
capabilities.recommendedNextEnactment: Reuse registry and permission metadata; if MCP is required, add an explicitly scoped transport and prove auth, tool allowlists, audit, tenant isolation, and failure behavior.

capabilities.name: Existing tests and verification coverage
capabilities.currentImplementation: Broad backend tests cover server config, platform foundation, event fabric, auth, logistics security, AI federation, agents, evaluation, and selected database behavior. Frontend module registry has tests.
capabilities.apiServicePath: Test suites exercise selected units/integrations; a complete live grid UI-to-source trace is not present.
capabilities.dataSource: Mostly test fixtures, mocks, and local services; live source certification tests not demonstrated.
capabilities.persistence: Database test coverage is selected rather than comprehensive operational data lifecycle proof.
capabilities.runtimeBehavior: Tests provide useful infrastructure and contract coverage, not proof of live grid operational correctness.
productionRisks: Missing live SCADA/EMS, GIS, production solver, browser Command Center, end-to-end realtime, full tenant-isolation, and provenance tests.
capabilities.recommendedNextEnactment: Extend existing test harnesses with source contract tests, live/disconnected/stale mode tests, UI-to-API integration tests, transport delivery, authorization and tenant isolation, and engineering-reviewed expected results.

capabilities.name: Mock/simulation versus real data-source boundaries
capabilities.currentImplementation: Simulation provider naming and freshness markers exist; mock SCADA telemetry, in-memory reference topology, fixed server telemetry, synthetic logistics data, and AI fallback-shaped results are present. Provenance is not shown to be mandatory and consistent across every response/consumer.
capabilities.apiServicePath: Multiple independent providers and fallback paths feed UI/API consumers; a common source-mode contract across all of them is not demonstrated.
capabilities.dataSource: Mix of fixed/mock/synthetic/reference data and configured external providers; default grid operational source not demonstrated.
capabilities.persistence: Varies by provider; source provenance retention is inconsistent/unproven.
capabilities.runtimeBehavior: Simulation/fallback data may make views appear populated despite unavailable operational sources.
testCoverage: Selected provider and AI tests; no universal provenance contract test demonstrated.
productionRisks: Users could confuse plausible generated data with operational state.
Provider 'connected' semantics may be false for mock adapters.
Fallback success-shaped responses obscure dependency failure.
capabilities.recommendedNextEnactment: Make source mode and provenance a mandatory shared contract; ensure all mock/simulation data is unmistakably labeled and cannot claim operational connectivity.

reusableInfrastructure: Existing Command Center frontend modules and map/visualization components
Existing Digital Twin model, service, and engine decomposition
Database lifecycle, migrations, repositories, outbox, and idempotency
Event schemas, API, bus, and WebSocket handler
Authentication, authorization, audit, policy, and governance primitives
AI runtime, federation, agents, safety, evaluation, and internal tool registry
Existing backend test and evaluation harnesses
recommendedEnactmentSequence: Define explicit mock, simulation, staging, and operational source modes.
Connect and certify one real or staging SCADA/EMS source through the existing data fabric.
Require source, timestamp/freshness, quality, connection, authority, and mode provenance on every grid response.
Establish one versioned authoritative topology and controlled synchronization without fabricated data.
Wire existing realtime transport and event persistence into normal startup and test end-to-end delivery/replay.
Validate outage, contingency, restoration, and analytics assumptions/solvers with engineering owners.
Harden credentials, endpoint authorization, tenant isolation, durable audit, production persistence, and readiness reporting.
Ground future AI in governed grid sources/tools with provenance, permission checks, audit, evaluation, and human approval.

safeToExtend: Existing Command Center UI and visualization components
Digital Twin engines as a reference/simulation platform
Data-fabric interfaces once real providers are implemented and verified
Event schemas/APIs and tested event-bus behavior
needsHardening: SCADA provider semantics and runtime wiring
Topology authority and duplicate canonical data
Data provenance, freshness, quality, source mode, and operational readiness
Token/password handling, route authorization consistency, and tenant isolation
Durable domain audit, production persistence, AI fallback signaling, engineering validation, and test coverage
blocked: Operational live-grid state and authoritative outage/switching until a real source and safe integration are established
Operationally valid state-based studies until source and solver validation
Authoritative event replay until complete durable ingestion/retention is proven
Operational AI engineering claims until grounded sources, governed tools, and evaluation are validated
missing: Demonstrated live SCADA/EMS protocol integration in default Command Center path
Demonstrated end-to-end operational restoration execution path
Demonstrated fully wired and tested Command Center WebSocket/SSE consumer path
Demonstrated externally exposed Command Center MCP service
